data.title: Bard-Parker handle
data.summary: Blades & scalpels · Flat reusable handle onto whose grooved tip a disposable surgical blade is mounted to form a scalpel.
data.body:
![Bard-Parker handle](instruments/bard-parker-handle.jpg)

_Also called: BP handle, Scalpel handle_

Flat reusable handle onto whose grooved tip a disposable surgical blade is mounted to form a scalpel.

## Parts
- Long flat body (often with metric ruler)
- Grooved, tapered blunt tip that receives the blade

## Types / variants
- No. 3 handle - small blades 10, 11, 12, 15 (Khopkar)
- No. 4 handle - large blades 20-25
- Longer versions marked L (3L, 4L)
- Other handles: No. 7, Siegel (round-bodied, held like a pen), Beaver (PPT1)

## Uses / indications
- Mounting a surgical blade for incision, excision, shave and other procedures

## How to hold
Pencil grip for fine dermatological incisions; table-knife grip for long firm cuts; violin-bow grip for long light strokes.

## Method of use
1. Attach: hold blade with artery forceps/needle holder, slide its slot onto the grooved tip until it clicks
2. Remove: lift the blade heel with the forceps and push it off the tip away from you

## Sterilisation & care
Autoclave, hot air oven, 2% glutaraldehyde or boiling

## Viva points & tips
- Never load or unload blades with fingers
- Seminar lists blade 9 also fitting No. 3; Khopkar says 10, 11, 12, 15
